item.caption: REWIND
item.help: This option allows you to rewind the game if you get killed by a monster, or if you make any other mistake. Use the HOTKEY + LEFT command within the game to rewind.

item.caption: SOFTPATCHING
item.help:
Choose strategy

AUTO: auto apply default patch

LAUNCH LAST: always launch the last one (can be modified in edit game menu)

SELECT: choose manually which patch to apply. Default one or patches in [ROM_NAME]-patches directory

DISABLED: never apply patch

item.caption: SHOW SAVE STATES ON START
item.help: Display the available save states before launching a game.

item.caption: AUTO SAVE/LOAD
item.help: Auto save the state when you quit a game, and auto load last saved state when you start a game.

item.caption: PRESS TWICE TO QUIT GAME
item.help: Press the buttons twice to end the game and go back to the main menu.

item.caption: GAME BOY MODE
item.help: Set the Super GameBoy mode for GameBoy games.

item.caption: GAME RATIO
item.help: The game ratio is the ratio between image width and image height. Use AUTO to let the emulator choose the original game ratio, that will give you the best retrogaming experience.

item.caption: RECALBOX OVERLAYS
item.help: On wide screens, display system images that wrap around emulated screen.

item.caption: SMOOTH GAMES
item.help: Smooth the game image. This option makes the image smoother, using bilinear filtering.

item.caption: INTEGER SCALE (PIXEL PERFECT)
item.help: Integer scaling is scaling by a factor of a whole number, such as 2x, 3x, 4x, etc. This option scales the image up to the greatest integer scale below the set resolution. So for instance, if you set your fullscreen resolution to 1920x1080 and enable integer scaling, it will only scale a 320x240 image up to 1280x960, and leave black borders all around. This is to maintain a 1:1 pixel ratio with the original source image, so that pixels are not unevenly duplicated.

item.caption: SHADERS SET
item.help: Shaders are like filters for the game rendering. You can select a shader set here, which is a collection of shaders selected for each system. You can also change the shader within the game with HOTKEY + L2 or HOTKEY + R2.

item.caption: ADVANCED SHADERS
item.help: Shaders are like filters for the game rendering. You can select a raw shader file here. This setting may be overridden by the shader set if it is not set to 'none'.

item.caption: HD MODE
item.help: Improves resolution on compatible 3d emulators. May have an impact on performance. (Dreamcast, Naomi, Atomiswave, Playstation, Saturn)

item.caption: WIDESCREEN (16/9)
item.if: (!hardware.crt or hardware.rrgbd2) and (board.ispcboard or board.ispi5board or board.ispi4board or board.issteamdeck)
item.help: Enables 16:9 hacks for compatible emulators. May have an impact on performance. (Dreamcast, Naomi, Atomiswave, Snes, Megadrive)

item.caption: AUTO BLITTER (FBNEO/MAME)
item.help: Enables automatic blitter and CPU settings for fbneo and mame games. Can enhance emulation precision on games like Cave.

item.caption: ENABLE VULKAN DRIVER
item.help: Enable the Vulkan driver when available. Enabled by default on RPi4, RPi5, and PC. Set to OFF if Dreamcast, Naomi or Atomiswave stop running.
item.grayedHelp: No vulkan driver is available on your hardware.

item.caption: RETROACHIEVEMENTS
item.help: Enable or disable RetroAchievements in games.

item.caption: HARDCORE MODE
item.help: Hardcore mode disables *all* savestate and rewind functions within the emulator: you will not be able to save and reload at any time. You will have to complete the game and get the achievements first time, just like on the original console. In reward for this, you will earn both the standard and the hardcore achievement, in effect earning double points! A regular game worth 400 points, is now worth 800 if you complete it on hardcore! For example: if you complete the game for 400 points, you then have the opportunity to earn another 400 on hardcore.
